technical_hypothesis.interaction_pattern: human-in-the-loop case prioritization before payroll or HR processing
technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: historical correction, escalation and reopening labels are often created after specialist handling and may leak final diagnosis, resolution, payroll impact or revised employee status into prediction-time features

training_data.observation_unit: one absence, return or employee-service case at the initial administrative review cutoff
training_data.input_data: pre-cutoff event type, dates, employee status, work schedule, prior related events, source system, completeness flags, queue, known deadlines and integration status; availability and consistency are unknown
training_data.target_or_reward: later administrative correction, reopening, reassignment, eSocial rejection or specialist escalation; definitions vary by organization
training_data.label_source: HCM, payroll, eSocial messaging, case-management and workflow audit events; cross-system linkage quality is unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before case assignment, payroll close or eSocial transmission
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and organization-dependent; rare event types and smaller employers may not support reliable local training
training_data.class_balance: unknown; material exceptions are expected to be less frequent than routine cases
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; policy, vendor, taxonomy and integration changes can make older cases non-comparable
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based validation with holdouts across payroll cycles and policy or system changes; site or business-unit grouped tests where transfer is claimed
training_data.leakage_risks: using final resolution, revised dates, specialist assignment, payroll reopening, medical conclusion, accepted eSocial response or fields populated after initial triage
training_data.representativeness_risks: collective agreements, work schedules, benefit regimes, organization size, occupational-health process, payroll vendor and local HR maturity vary materially
training_data.feedback_loop: prioritization changes who reviews a case and how quickly corrections occur, altering the observed label and potentially reinforcing queues with historically greater attention
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: absence and health-adjacent records require strict minimization, purpose limitation, role-based access and LGPD controls; the model must not infer health condition, fitness, discipline or employability
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use eSocial validation rules, mandatory fields, overlap checks, deterministic deadlines, integration reconciliation, configured escalation rules and specialist review queues

portfolio_comparison.reason: The remaining classifier only ranks administrative exception or escalation risk. It does not introduce a distinct HR outcome beyond existing structured HCM, eSocial validation, case-routing and escalation capabilities, and it risks duplicating generic supervised triage patterns already represented elsewhere.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt or configure HCM absence management, eSocial validations, case routing and escalation rules. Consider a local classifier only after deterministic controls are exhausted and incremental value over built-in case prediction is demonstrated.

research.findings: Current eSocial guidance shows that missing or conflicting return events can block later absences and payroll remuneration, confirming an operational need. However, the core controls are deterministic and current HCM and HR-service platforms already support leave and return workflows, traceability, routing, escalation, service prediction and estimated resolution time. No materially distinct opportunity remains.
